title: French students and unions stage nationwide protests
seoTitle: Paris nationwide protests over cost of living

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against poor school teaching conditions, rising fuel prices, and the high cost of living.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand more teachers, improved learning conditions, and action on fuel and living costs.
tea.changed: Oct 17: Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu reported 1,200 arrests after nationwide demonstrations.

summary: Students and various leftist unions staged nationwide protests across France, including in Paris, to demand better teaching conditions, relief from rising fuel prices, and a lower cost of living. Organised in cities across the country following earlier demonstrations regarding teacher shortages, the action drew an estimated 550,000 participants. While many marches proceeded peacefully, French authorities reported widespread vandalism, looting, and arson in cities such as Marseille, Lyon, and Limoges. Government officials blamed far-left and ultra-left groups for instigating violence and clashes with law enforcement, while left-wing figures defended the mobilisation as largely calm. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu and Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez condemned the destruction, vowing strict punishment and accountability for vandals.
demands: Relief for the cost of living
response: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez blamed radical left groups for stoking violence, while Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu condemned arson and looting. Officials reported numerous arrests and injuries to law enforcement personnel.

crowd.text: An estimated 550,000 people took part in demonstrations across France

updates.text: French students and unions organized nationwide demonstrations drawing an estimated 550,000 protesters.
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu stated that 1,200 people had been arrested following nationwide unrest.
